name: reasoning-discipline-not-verified
description: ADMITTED GAP: a REASONING_MESSAGE_CONTENT with no opener is tolerated — the specification's Note on the reasoning page records that a consumer is not yet required to detect a streaming-discipline violation on reasoning messages or spans, because the reference implementation verifies that discipline for text messages and tool calls but not for reasoning, and requiring detection would declare a shipped consumer non-conformant; the producer is non-conformant either way. This pins what a consumer actually does today: the orphaned fragment is dropped, the run carries on, and no reasoning message is materialised
kill: add open/close verification for reasoning messages and spans — a deliberate change, not a repair: this fixture and the Note it quotes must be revised in the same commit, the fixture flipping to a failed outcome as the Note is withdrawn. Until then, making the orphan fatal breaks this fixture while the Note still says a consumer need not detect it

dotnet.intentional: The same admitted gap, one step wider on this lane: .NET also does not verify reasoning discipline, but it does not drop the orphaned fragment either — REASONING_MESSAGE_CONTENT yields a reasoning-content update whether or not an opener preceded it, so an extra message survives. Microsoft.Extensions.AI carries reasoning as TextReasoningContent, which AsAGUIMessages does not project into `content`.

typescript.intentional: the TypeScript reducer says out loud that it dropped the orphaned fragment, which is what makes 'tolerated' distinguishable from 'silently swallowed'; the .NET lane has no equivalent reducer-level warning, so only the tolerance itself is required of both
